evidence.primary_claim: Airi describes intense difficulty with eye contact, crowds and relationships, adopting a facade while privately desiring connection.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Opening Sakura first-person interior monologue: subjectively describes a social facade and wish for connection; cannot quantify enduring competence. Narrative date undetermined; do not assign the inner monologue's background to 30 June.

evidence.primary_claim: Airi sees Sudō standing over three injured boys and quietly photographs the apparent end of their fight.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Sakura personally narrates photographing three injured students and Sudō's blows; the short exposure does not reveal all prior provocations.

evidence.primary_claim: Airi freezes with fear then evades Sudō without being identified; he senses a nearby presence.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Her freezing, careful exit and Sudō's unanswered suspicion are narrated; he does not identify Sakura then.

evidence.primary_claim: The phone S-System app displays class and private points, supports private-point transfers, and applies a monthly distribution described as 100 times class points.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: First-person Kiyotaka explains the S-Point app, transfer and 100x monthly relation; note this is a July exposition, not each student's April knowledge.

evidence.primary_claim: Class D fell from 1000 to zero class points earlier in the year; Kiyotaka recalls a specially negotiated purchase of Sudō's midterm point.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: July recollection of earlier 1000-to-zero class scores and special test-point purchase; no general right to buy arbitrary grade outcomes.

evidence.primary_claim: The July point board shows Class A at 1004 and Class D at 87; other classes also gained points, so Suzune cautions the ranking gap remains.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Class A's 1004 and Class D's 87 are shown; Horikita's concern about other classes' gains is her reasoning.

evidence.primary_claim: Hirata notes Class D avoided ordinary conduct deductions; Chabashira reports a first-year delay in private-point distribution amid unresolved trouble.
evidence.epistemic_note: Attribution is the speaker's statement, not independently established world truth.
evidence.review_note: Hirata infers that recent behavioral deductions did not recur; Chabashira directly reports payment delay, but her motive remains undisclosed.

evidence.primary_claim: Kiyotaka notes Airi's isolation, Kōenji's comfort alone, and Suzune's use of free supermarket ingredients to prepare lunch.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Observations of solitude and Suzune's cooking are through Kiyotaka's narration; his judgments about Kōenji's motives remain subjective.

evidence.primary_claim: Chabashira summons Sudō from class (p.22); later Suzune questions whether delayed private-point deposits reflect student trouble rather than a school fault (p.23).
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Sudō is called after class on p22; Suzune's p23 explanation about why money is late is a question, not known causation.

evidence.primary_claim: Suzune does not participate in the class chat and mutes notifications; she later distances herself from Kushida, while Kiyotaka describes increased ease speaking to Suzune.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Group chat nonparticipation, muting and Suzune's spoken dislike of Kushida are supported; Kiyotaka's comfort is self-reported, not proof of mutual intimacy.

evidence.primary_claim: Sudō says other students obtained duplicate keycards to Kiyotaka's locked dorm room without his knowledge; Kushida also shows a copy and offers its return.
evidence.epistemic_note: Attribution is the speaker's statement, not independently established world truth.
evidence.review_note: Sudō's statement and physical keycard plus Kushida's key confirm duplicated access; do not infer that all holders had consent.

evidence.primary_claim: Sudō reports fighting three Class C students and fearing long suspension; his version of instigation remains disputed.
evidence.epistemic_note: Attribution is the speaker's statement, not independently established world truth.
evidence.review_note: Sudō reports the complaint and suspension prospect; truth of self-defense is not yet adjudicated.

evidence.primary_claim: Sudō says he is the only first-year being considered for a regular basketball role; selection is not yet final.
evidence.epistemic_note: Attribution is the speaker's statement, not independently established world truth.
evidence.review_note: Sudō says regular basketball status was only a nomination under consideration; never mark him definitively selected.

evidence.primary_claim: Sudō alleges Komiya and Kondou lured him to a special building with Ishizaki and threatened his basketball participation before the physical confrontation.
evidence.epistemic_note: Attribution is the speaker's statement, not independently established world truth.
evidence.review_note: Sudō supplies the alleged lure and intimidation involving Komiya, Kondou and Ishizaki; instigation remains an interested party claim.

evidence.primary_claim: Sudō says the school gave him until next Tuesday to produce evidence or face suspension until summer and a class-point penalty; no precise penalty is stated.
evidence.epistemic_note: Attribution is the speaker's statement, not independently established world truth.
evidence.review_note: The school deadline, suspension and class penalty are conveyed by Sudō, without fixed numerical amounts or universal disciplinary rule.

evidence.primary_claim: Kiyotaka questions how Sudō's use of force would be weighed against a self-defense argument; Kushida suggests obtaining a confession or finding an eyewitness.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Kiyotaka's skepticism about self-defense differs from a legal ruling; Kushida explicitly proposes recantation or eyewitness search.

evidence.primary_claim: Sudō requests discretion because of basketball risks; Kushida and Kiyotaka encourage him to avoid personally conducting the inquiry.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Sudō's confidentiality request is grounded in basketball concerns and friends advise noninvolvement; no durable behavioral improvement proven.

evidence.primary_claim: Chabashira discloses the Class C complaint and possible consequences to Class D without establishing who started the fight.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Teacher states the two-class physical dispute and suspended judgment; this establishes investigation, not guilt.

evidence.primary_claim: Suzune initially declines to rescue Sudō and considers whether shielding him from consequences would hinder behavioral change.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Horikita's refusal is directly voiced during lunch; self-improvement theory is her conditional evaluation of Sudō's behavior.

evidence.primary_claim: Hirata and Karuizawa lead one witness-search group and Kushida another; they set out despite limited time, with no result yet established on this page.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: At p54 two teams are organized to search, not yet proven to have interviewed every student or received reliable answers.

evidence.primary_claim: Kushida asks Kiyotaka to help persuade Suzune, follows Suzune, and receives her continued refusal.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Kushida tries to win Horikita's assistance, who refuses again on p56; no persuasive success is attributable here.

evidence.primary_claim: Kiyotaka proposes an inquiry with Class B rather than solely random campus searching.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Kiyotaka reasons Class B has an incentive against Class C and explicitly allows for hidden hostile plans; proposal not certainty.

evidence.primary_claim: Kushida approaches unfamiliar students in Class B with relative ease, unlike her intimidated companions.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Kushida recognizes acquaintances and socializes in Class B while others hesitate; observed contextual social fluency.

evidence.primary_claim: Hirata argues that protecting classmates and friendships can matter more than conserving class points at any cost.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Hirata explicitly weighs friendship against point preservation; do not encode an invariant sacrifice preference.

evidence.primary_claim: Chabashira announces an individual route to change classes through a private-point purchase distinct from class ranking.
evidence.epistemic_note: Attribution is the speaker's statement, not independently established world truth.
evidence.review_note: Chabashira says a personal-points route to changing class exists; she has not yet demonstrated a successful transfer.

evidence.primary_claim: Chabashira quotes twenty million private points as the transfer price for entering a chosen class; no successful transaction is shown.
evidence.epistemic_note: Attribution is the speaker's statement, not independently established world truth.
evidence.review_note: Twenty million is a teacher-stated price for chosen-class transfer; individual eligibility or settlement steps remain unobserved.

evidence.primary_claim: Chabashira reports that no one completed the transfer and recounts a past fraud case reaching almost twelve million points before expulsion.
evidence.epistemic_note: Attribution is the speaker's statement, not independently established world truth.
evidence.review_note: Chabashira's historical near-twelve-million fraud anecdote is reported testimony; do not independently assert record books verified.

evidence.primary_claim: Chabashira says individual club participation or competitive achievements can earn points, without disclosing any universal amount or algorithm.
evidence.epistemic_note: Attribution is the speaker's statement, not independently established world truth.
evidence.review_note: Club reward possibility is stated with a calligraphy example; neither routine participation nor a fixed stipend is guaranteed.

evidence.primary_claim: Kiyotaka argues that Sudō's prospective basketball contributions create a Class A incentive to keep him in school; Suzune considers that benefit.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Kiyotaka offers club contribution as a reason to keep Sudō; Horikita's acknowledgement is qualified and not full endorsement yet.

evidence.primary_claim: Suzune identifies Airi Sakura as a likely ignored witness through observations before Sakura makes an admission.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Horikita notices Sakura lowering her gaze during the call for witnesses; her certainty precedes any admission.

evidence.primary_claim: Kushida approaches Sakura, who initially resists discussing the fight and struggles with unfamiliar social attention.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Sakura averts her gaze and declines Kushida's question after school; withdrawal is observed, not evidence of intent to deceive.

evidence.primary_claim: Sudō lashes out while feeling abandoned by classmates; Suzune challenges both his conduct and the practical cost to Class D.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Sudō protests classmates' waning aid and Horikita's point tradeoff; note emotional reaction and no fixed actual penalty.

evidence.primary_claim: Kiyotaka points to existing classroom cameras but cannot confirm equivalent functioning cameras captured the special-building fight.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Kiyotaka points out classroom cameras; their use for class assessment is his inference, not blanket proof every hall is recorded.

evidence.primary_claim: Kiyotaka restrains Horikita from pressing Sakura, tells Sakura that testimony must be voluntary and offers help if she is intimidated; Sakura still denies witnessing the incident.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Kiyotaka prevents forcing Sakura and invites reporting threats despite her denial; her status is unresolved in this scene.

evidence.primary_claim: Ichinose approaches Kiyotaka and Horikita at the special building after hearing about the conflict and offers to help; Kiyotaka considers possible Class B incentives as speculation.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Ichinose's spontaneous encounter and offer are observed, but Class B interest and Kiyotaka's interpretations require uncertainty.

evidence.primary_claim: Class D accepts Ichinose's help; a Class D-only eyewitness may be regarded as biased.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Class D accepts Ichinose as an ally, with limited impartiality of its own witness; probability of another witness remains conjectural.

evidence.primary_claim: Ichinose brings Class B dorm residents' requests to the dorm manager and explains that she serves as an informal representative chosen within her class.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Ichinose interacts with dorm manager about requests and later states a Class B-only voluntary office; no school appointment.

evidence.primary_claim: Ichinose explains that Class B chose representative, deputy and secretary roles independently; they are not mandatory school-wide offices.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Class B representative, vice and secretary are Ichinose's descriptions; not compulsory formal governance of every class.

evidence.primary_claim: Ichinose passes along a rumor of a possible summer tropical-island trip without an exam specification or confirmed mechanism.
evidence.epistemic_note: Attribution is the speaker's statement, not independently established world truth.
evidence.review_note: Tropical-island summer trip is a rumor passed by Ichinose; absolutely no special-exam mechanism can be inferred.

evidence.primary_claim: Ichinose has received a written romantic confession and Chihiro confronts her about the unfamiliar boy she brought to their meeting; Ichinose hesitates and cannot easily lie.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Chihiro's written confession, meeting and distress are evidenced across pp123-126; the encounter is not a direct spoken new confession.

evidence.primary_claim: Ichinose acknowledges she mishandled Chihiro's feelings by avoidance; their future relationship is unresolved.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Ichinose openly admits mishandling Chihiro's feelings and reports asking to resume normal relations; there is no accepted reconciliation.

evidence.primary_claim: Kushida and Kiyotaka accompany Sakura to a campus electronics store for a camera repair; she fears the clerk.

evidence.review_note: The trio attend campus repair desk; Sakura shows anxiety and the repair clerk draws unwanted attention, observed separately.

evidence.primary_claim: Kiyotaka recognizes the clerk's troubling attention and offers his own repair contact instead of having Sakura leave sensitive details.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Kiyotaka redirects repair contact after noting the clerk's gaze; legally validating his explanation about warranty is out of scope.

evidence.primary_claim: Sakura reports loving photography since childhood; her father gave her a camera before junior high, but she does not claim technical expertise.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Sakura says she has liked cameras since youth and received a camera from her father; lack of technical expertise is self-described.

evidence.primary_claim: Kiyotaka contacts Sotomura (Professor) to request electronics advice because he cannot identify the appropriate device himself.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Kiyotaka phones Sotomura for technical input when choosing a device; source demonstrates task-specific help-seeking.

evidence.primary_claim: Sakura privately admits she witnessed Sudō's fight, explains her fear of attention, and explicitly promises Kushida to testify, though her resilience under future pressure is not established.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Sakura says she witnessed the fight and promises Kushida to testify on p146; pressure tolerance at hearing remains open.

evidence.primary_claim: Kushida notices Sakura's eyeglasses do not show usual prescription distortion; their purpose is only hypothesized at this point.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Kushida distinguishes glasses with and without lens distortion and hypothesizes concealment, which is an inference until later revelations.

evidence.primary_claim: On the eve of deliberation Class D has a witness and helpers, but still lacks irrefutable proof of Sudō's innocence.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Chapter-opening Kiyotaka narration records anxiety and lack of decisive proof despite class mobilization; predicts, not adjudicates, hearing.

evidence.primary_claim: Kanzaki reports posting a physical notice requesting information on the Sudō incident; he states he has received no useful leads from that approach.

evidence.epistemic_note: Attribution is the speaker's statement, not independently established world truth.

evidence.primary_claim: Kiyotaka describes how a temporary token from the S-System point page allows payment requests; he briefly notices an undisclosed portion of Ichinose's point screen. The amount and what it implies remain unconfirmed.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Kiyotaka explains point-transfer token issuing; a fleeting glimpse of Ichinose's screen is recorded but its numerical content is not disclosed.

evidence.primary_claim: Sakura reluctantly offers herself as a witness to Chabashira despite significant anxiety about speaking.

evidence.primary_claim: Kiyotaka explains Sakura must be free to decline and her testimony might not ensure acquittal.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.

evidence.primary_claim: Sakura states she does not know how to make friends and says she wanted to answer Kushida's earlier invitation but lacked the courage.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Sakura acknowledges longing for friends and her failure to answer Kushida's invitation; source is Sakura's private self-disclosure.

evidence.primary_claim: Kiyotaka counsels Sakura to testify for herself and the truth, not out of forced loyalty to Sudō or classmates.

evidence.review_note: Kiyotaka counsels speaking for the truth and Sakura's own sake, but she had already promised to testify, preventing a unique causal attribution.

evidence.primary_claim: Kushida discovers an online gravure-idol profile under the name Shizuku and identifies resemblance to Sakura.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Kushida discovers the online Shizuku pictures and identifies visual resemblance; does not alone establish publicly verified identity.

evidence.primary_claim: Photographic dorm details support the small group's identification of Sakura as Shizuku, without making her identity public.
evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Group identifies Sakura with Kiyotaka's specific dorm-door clue; shared disclosure stays limited, not a campus-wide revelation.

evidence.primary_claim: Sakura comes to school for the hearing despite fear and anxiety about expectations.

evidence.review_note: Sakura appears in class on hearing day despite anxiety, not proof she was already confident or had testified.

evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: The council president and Tachibana preside with teachers; procedural features are observations of this specific hearing.

evidence.primary_claim: Suzune probes inconsistencies in Class C's prepared account, including why the reputed fighter Ishizaki was present.

evidence.review_note: Suzune challenges Class C's inconsistent placement of Ishizaki; coordinated answers by opponents do not mean fault proven.

evidence.primary_claim: Sakura speaks unusually forcefully under pressure, but Sakagami challenges her late disclosure and potential partiality, so her testimony alone does not resolve fault.

evidence.primary_claim: Sakagami observes that the photos do not establish who initiated the altercation even if Sakura was present.

evidence.primary_claim: Suzune distinguishes a need for Sudō to reflect on his past from whether he deserves punishment for this specific disputed incident.

evidence.primary_claim: Ichinose and Kanzaki await news from the hearing and consider further assistance after the first confrontation fails to settle the allegation.

evidence.primary_claim: Ichinose recognizes ethical tension in a proposed deceptive tactic but remains willing to consider it for this case.

evidence.primary_claim: Suzune considers gradual social growth for Sakura beneficial but cautions against forcing her beyond present ability.

evidence.review_note: Suzune suggests gradual social exposure without excessive demands on Sakura; this is a situational caution not a clinical rule.

evidence.primary_claim: Kiyotaka arranges for Kushida to send appealing emails to lure Ishizaki, Komiya and Kondou to the special building; Ichinose appears as they attempt to leave.

evidence.primary_claim: Ichinose draws attention to a hallway camera, inducing uncertainty about possible recorded evidence.

evidence.primary_claim: The parties head to the council room after their special-building confrontation, with the complainants' access to outside advice constrained.

evidence.review_note: Chabashira uses uniform entrance scores and covert activity to raise suspicion; her 'trap' phrasing is her interpretation, not proved motives.

evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Manabu references an open student council secretary place and offers it to Kiyotaka; he refuses and claims preference for an ordinary life.

evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Suzune retrospectively accuses Kiyotaka of steering the camera plan; he denies it, so do not record the full thought sequence as directly observed.

evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.

evidence.epistemic_note: Confirm speaker, episode timing, factual limits and actor-knowledge acquisition.
evidence.review_note: Kiyotaka's inner monologue forecasts difficulties from Class B and a suspected Ryūen threat; future outcomes are not predetermined world facts.

behavioral_cases.review_note: Sakura actively chooses camera use and retreat during an emotionally overwhelming encounter; no claim she saw or understood the initial provocation.
Sudō demonstrably emerges uninjured against three hurt opponents, but that scene supports a local combat outcome rather than a moral/legal verdict.
Sudō asks for discretion and complies with friends' request to stay away; not evidence of a stable compliant personality.
Suzune initially says no and later reevaluates potential future point gains, a conditional tactical shift rather than immediate promise of aid.
Kushida coordinates witnesses and can talk to Class B acquaintances, while other searchers' acts cannot be counted as her personal feats.
Kiyotaka targets Class B on strategic ranking incentives but explicitly considers their ability to exploit Class D too.
Hirata states a priority for peers in this controversy; a spoken preference is not a universal decision policy.
Suzune notices Sakura's unusual gaze avoidance after an inquiry and makes an accurate later-confirmed hypothesis, not omniscient detection.
Kushida invites and supports Sakura, and accompanies the repair outing; Sakura's independent later decision is not fully caused by Kushida.
Ichinose acts as an informal class delegate for dorm requests, and explicitly says Class B created those roles itself.
Ichinose admits mishandling the confession and asks Chihiro to relate normally; evidence cannot establish restored friendship or romance.
Kiyotaka observes disturbing clerk attention and uses his own personal details on a repair form; not a universal right to alter ownership fields.
Sakura privately admits she saw the fight and specifically promises to testify on p146; this is an affirmative commitment, not merely tentative help.
Kanzaki's printed notice yields no useful lead, whereas a different online channel produces a tip later shared by Ichinose; Kanzaki evaluates that hearsay.
Kiyotaka proposes truthful self-directed testimony and Sakura thanks him; she had already promised to testify, so sole-cause persuasion is unwarranted.
Kushida personally connects Shizuku's look to Sakura; Kiyotaka independently identifies a dorm-door clue, which must not become her own demonstrated feat.
Sakura attends and testifies under pressure, submitting photos of presence and aftermath; this demonstrates situational courage without establishing fault at the start.
Suzune presses inconsistencies and insists current fault must be evaluated independently of Sudō's past; the first hearing does not secure acquittal.
Ichinose herself directs the staged-camera threat to the accusers, while the actual purchase and installation involved other people.
Kiyotaka contributes to a coordinated camera deception and uses supposed council knowledge, but success depends on Horikita's planning and others' installation.
Ishizaki initially maintains a self-harming bargaining position but later backs down; do not freeze the first statement as a stable utility weight.
Kiyotaka and Ichinose document and interrupt real harassment; his threatening language must not be confused with a legal action or universal safety strategy.
Sudō admits consequences of prior aggression and promises change; Chabashira immediately challenges the durability of his repentance.
Manabu directly offers a vacant secretary seat after querying Tachibana; this is a concrete offer but not a general automatic hiring rule.
Kiyotaka explicitly refuses council membership and offers a subjective desire for quiet, which may not explain all subsequent choices.
Kiyotaka denies steering Suzune and minimizes his involvement; the unidentified male's separate remarks are not his behavioral feat.
Kiyotaka personally arranges Kushida's emails and awaits three complainants; Kushida's actual transmission and Ichinose's later blocking remain separate actor actions.
